items.article: Connor is motivated by a desire to give his son Alfie 'a childhood he didn't have' An ex-soldier who began his small side hustle 'for some extra cash' in lockdown now earns up to £40,000 a month and has quit his full-time job. He said his new business has allowed him to give his son "a childhood (he) didn’t have", which he says is "worth more than anything". Connor Stone, 31, joined the British Army in 2019 and began reselling hard-to-find items, including hair clippers, weights and outdoor heaters, during the Covid-19 pandemic. He gradually began selling clothes from his "own wardrobe" too, making a "few hundred" pounds a month, before leaving the Army in 2024 for a "fresh start" after he and his wife Lauren, 32, suffered seven miscarriages while struggling to conceive. Connor took a job in logistics at DHL while continuing to resell, eventually joining Whatnot - a live- shopping marketplace - and began to sell items in seconds. Within six months, he said he was making in a week what he earned in a month at DHL, prompting him to quit his job and pursue reselling full-time. He now sells around 300 items a day, hosts five livestreams a week and works with suppliers across the globe, while he and Lauren welcomed their son Alfie (now 11 months) in October 2025. Connor is now looking forward to taking Alfie to Disneyland for his first birthday with his earnings, and hopes to grow the business even further. items.article: Kick-off times, team news, TV coverage and everything else you need to know ahead of this weekend's games in the BKT United Rugby Championship. It was a tough start for the four Irish provinces last week, as Connacht, Ulster, Leinster and Munster were all beaten in the opening round. Fortunately, the Irish teams have been able to welcome back some of their Ireland internationals this week, as they look to pick up wins and finally get their seasons up and running. Connacht were the only province to miss out on any bonus points in their opening game, and they travel to Italy on Friday night to take on a Benetton side who drew at home to the Dragons. Then on Saturday, Leinster are in Durban to complete their South African tour, as Leo Cullen's side face the Sharks at 5.30pm, while at the same time Ulster have a tough challenge away to Glasgow Warriors. In the late kick-off, Munster welcome the Bulls to Thomond Park, as they look to start moving upwards after the resignation on Thursday of CEO Ian Flanagan . items.text: I asked my husband to marry me after just 4 weeks, but I wouldn't like if my daughter did the same
items.article: Usually when people get engaged it's a cause for celebration. But when I announced my engagement, the reaction from my friends and family was largely 'What?!' Not to mention, 'Who?' Usually when people get engaged it’s a cause for celebration. Family members crack open champagne, and friends video call to celebrate. But when I announced my engagement, the reaction from my friends and family was largely ‘What?!’ Not to mention, ‘Who?’ Yes, who. Because my loved ones had not yet met the man I’d asked to marry me. To be honest, I barely knew him myself. I met Sam in November 2019 and four weeks later, I proposed. It might be surprising he said yes, given we were still relative strangers. Even more surprising is that, seven years on, we’re still together. We celebrated our sixth wedding anniversary last month. I was 31 when we met, and Sam 43. At the time, I was in a weird place. After living in New York with my then-boyfriend of five years, I’d left in a hurry after being fired from a job I loathed and breaking up with said boyfriend after growing apart. Fleeing to London , I’d ended up in a cupboard-sized room in a house share in Camberwell with two girls I barely knew.

items.article: On a Fourth Wing hangover? Here are the best romantasy books to read next, from spicy stories to beloved classics The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice . There comes a time in every avid reader’s life when they must put away serious things and take up more (im)mature ones. Rebecca Yarros’ Fourth Wing was the first novel to shift my perspective on the BookTok-dubbed genre of ‘romantasy’. While I’m not hailing it as a piece of prized literature, I can safely declare it to be an enthralling book with well-developed characters and the perfect balance of romance and fantasy. Chances are you agree, or else you wouldn’t have landed on this article. Yarros’ latest instalment, Threshing Day , was released on 29 September – and if you’ve already torn through its 13 stories, you’re in the right place. Read more: New Fourth Wing book, Threshing Day, has landed with 50% off There’s something inherently healing about loosening one’s grasp on high literature and delving into the murky depths of high fantasy and romance instead. This isn’t to say that some novels which fall within the genre are not, or cannot be, considered high-brow classics – far from it.

items.article: WARNING, DISTRESSING CONTENT After Death Row inmate Christa Pike survived two lethal injections on Wednesday evening (September 30), a doctor has claimed it was doomed from the beginning A top doctor has outlined exactly why Death Row inmate Christa Pike didn’t die during the horrific botched execution attempt and warned she may be too ill to be killed. The convicted murderer was set to be executed by lethal injection in the state of Tennessee on Wednesday (September 30). Pike – who had a last ditch request for clemency refused by Governor Bill Lee – was strapped to the gurney as a team of officials attempted to find a vein for the lethal drug. But after two failed doses of the drug, Pike was reportedly left “thrashing” on the gurney and was later rushed to hospital with potentially life-altering brain damage. Dr. Joel Zivot, a vocal opponent of capital punishment and a member of Pike’s defence team, explained how he believed the execution attempt was doomed from the start. “Lethal injection is not a medical act – and it's a difficult thing to administer,” he said. Dr Zivot revealed that lethal injection involves inserting an intravenous catheter (IV), a delicate procedure performed by trained professionals.

items.text: Dippy eggs or Angel Delight? Here are the UK’s most popular nostalgic foods
items.article: Dippy eggs remain popular for adults – even sometimes being used to cure hangovers Classic dishes such as beans on toast, "dippy" eggs and fish fingers are among the nation's favourite childhood comfort foods, a survey has found. A poll of 2,000 Britons asking for their most nostalgic meals also featured shepherd's pie, fairy cakes, rice pudding and apple crumble with custard. Claiming the top spot were "dippy" eggs and soldiers, comprising a soft-boiled egg alongside buttered toast sliced into fingers. Writer and culinary history consultant Sue Bailey has offered insight as to why some foods prompt such personal memories. "Personal nostalgia is a strong emotion linked to the familiar taste and smell of food , particularly based on comforting foods when a child," she said. items.text: My Son Wanted to Be a Content Creator: The Cost of Chasing Online Fame
items.article: At first, Alex's interest in social media seemed harmless. But it spiraled into obsession and then, on his 20th birthday, he died by suicide. My son, Alexander, became fascinated with YouTube when he was about 10 years old. Like millions of children, he began by watching entertaining videos—sports highlights, challenges and creators whose lives appeared exciting and free. But YouTube was not simply a collection of videos that Alex chose to watch. Its algorithm studied him. It learned what held his attention and kept offering him more. At first, it seemed harmless. Then homework began taking longer, bedtime became later and stopping became difficult. There was always another video. Alex would say that he needed only one more minute, but one video led to another and then another. We had rules in our home, including leaving phones on the counter at night. But ordinary household rules were not designed to compete with platforms engineered to keep children engaged. The phone was only the object. The real power was inside it: the endless feed, the recommendations, the notifications and the promise that something even more exciting was about to appear. As Alex grew older, YouTube was joined by TikTok, Snapchat and other platforms. He was no longer satisfied with watching other people. He wanted to become a content creator himself. items.text: Air travel expert gives verdict on three key issues of the Flydubai plane hijacking
items.article: The aviation security expert said that there is no universal background check system for pilots The alleged hijacking of an Israel-bound flight has raised questions over how secure the vetting process is for one of aviation's most skilled jobs. Flydubai FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv rapidly descended during a terrifying ordeal as the co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the plane after attacking his fellow pilot with an axe, or possibly stabbing him. It is still unclear why the co-pilot to acted in this way. Yet the question remains: how was this person able to bypass rigorous background checks and be given the responsibility of flying planes? "It's very easy after every incident to say, what more can we do?" Phillip Baum, visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, said. "Often, airline pilots are recruited from other states, so the degree of background checks is somewhat limited. They'll certainly have their pilot training and licenses, but in terms of background checks from other states, it's always a problem." Mr Baum, who has 35 years' experience in aviation security, explained that varying pilot-vetting models across countries have long created issues for the aviation industry.
